Item: Zip to district disambiguation
Detail: Zips cross district lines. After zip entry, show the districts that overlap it and let the user pick the one they actually live in.
Notes: Zip is orientation only, never district truth. 2026-08-11: M03 makes the problem visible - turn on Show districts and a zip straddling a boundary is now something a reader can see rather than something the docs assert. Note the overlay file is the 1:500000 cartographic generalization and is for display only; deciding which district an address actually falls in is a server-side job against full-resolution geometry, so M02 must not point-in-polygon against public/geo/cd119.geojson. 2026-08-12. Click-to-select shipped. map.queryRenderedFeatures across every active fill layer with a 3px slop box; one hit selects directly, several open a disambiguation prompt grouped by tier, zero is a no-op rather than a cleared selection so clicking empty water does not silently drop what a reader chose. The prompt is never a two-option prompt - it lists however many districts actually contain the point. Verified by screenshot: 85701 returns 6 (municipal, school, county, state house, state senate, congressional) and 07866 returns 7 including TWO school districts side by side. This is the surface that makes the zip rule real: the reader clicks to choose a district, nothing is inferred from where their zip centroid fell. Selection is feature-state, never a source mutation. tests/district-hits.test.ts covers the three hard cases against the committed boundary files. Two bugs found and fixed during this work, both surfaced by the map error logging added under M08: a line-width expression nested zoom inside a case, which is invalid (zoom is only legal as the direct input of a top-level step or interpolate) so MapLibre rejected the whole layer and boundaries silently lost their width; and because that throw left the fill layer added without its line, a single is-it-present guard on the line layer let every later pass re-add the fill and log Layer already exists forever - each layer is now guarded individually. Item: Voting records - state
Detail: Plural Open (ex-Open States). All 50 states, API plus bulk download.
Notes: AUTHOR CLEARANCE 2026-08-12: the author approved building against this source when asked, which is the CLAUDE.md ask-before-adding-an-external-source gate for it. Legistar, Diligent Community, Congress.gov and Plural Open were all cleared in the same answer. Clearance is to build the adapter; it is NOT a finding for D14 and does not answer B09, both of which still stand. 2026-08-12: not started, but the shape it plugs into now exists - lib/officials/types.ts and the officeholders-us.json artifact pattern. Per brief 5.0a fetch PER STATE (AZ NJ NH, the states with boundary coverage) and write officeholders-04/33/34.json so adding a state is adding a file. Prefer the CC-0 bulk download over the API for the same reasons the Congress adapter does. sldu/sldl divisions are already in the registry (25 sldu + 58 sldl matched) and are where these attach; remember AZ elects one senator and TWO representatives per legislative district, so the many-to-many join is load-bearing from the first row. 2026-08-12 ROSTER SHIPPED, VOTES NOT - same split as D02. lib/sources/plural/, officeholders-04/33/34.json, tests/plural.test.ts 12 tests. Committed directly onto main as 9af2fbc and 59fd858 - no feature branch, which was a slip: the session had checked out main to read test counts after the PR #13 ship and never branched again. Recorded rather than tidied over, because a tracker that names a branch which never existed is the kind of small untruth this column exists to prevent. Evidence: test (129 pass), lint and build all green. BUILT ON THE NIGHTLY BULK CSV, NOT THE v3 API: data.openstates.org/people/current/<st>.csv, one file per state, NO KEY AND NO LOGIN REQUIRED, verified live for az/nj/nh (200, 84KB/119KB/354KB). So PLURAL_API_KEY is NOT needed for the roster - it is for the API, which this does not touch. Data is CC-0; attribution is requested not required and is carried anyway. 620 legislators fetched. THE NEW HAMPSHIRE TRAP, and it is the at-large trap again in a different costume. Plural designates NH House districts by county and number - "Merrimack 8", "Rockingham 30" - while this repo identifiers are Census numeric codes, sldl:608. A direct join scores 0 OF 201 and does so silently. The bridge is the registry own Census-sourced LABEL, which carries the statutory designation: sldl:608 is labelled "State House District Merrimack 08". indexDivisions() keys on state|chamber|normalized-designation and designationKey() strips zero-padding so "Merrimack 08" meets "Merrimack 8". This is NOT the name-string join CLAUDE.md forbids: that rule is about joining geographic entities on colloquial names that collide across states, whereas a NH House district designation IS its statutory identity, the match is scoped to one state and one chamber, it is exact after normalization rather than fuzzy, and every miss is reported. Output is keyed on this repo OCD-IDs throughout. RESULT, and the denominator matters: AZ 90 legislators / 24 linked, NJ 120 / 21, NH 410 / 85. The apparent shortfall is the THREE-COUNTY CLIP, not a mismatch - the registry holds 16 AZ, 14 NJ and 53 NH legislative districts, and ALL OF THEM now have someone. Zero holes. The build prints held-vs-covered per state precisely so a clip is never mistaken for a broken join. MANY-TO-MANY CONFIRMED IN REAL DATA: AZ LD19 returns one senator (David Gowan) and TWO representatives (Gail Griffin, Lupe Diaz); NJ Assembly District 25 returns two Assemblymembers; NH Merrimack 07 returns two. A one-district-per-seat column would have had to drop half of them. CHAMBER TITLES ARE A PER-STATE TABLE, not derived: NJ lower chamber is the General Assembly and its members are Assemblymembers, not Representatives. A state with no entry reports rather than inventing a title, same rule as the body registry refusing to mint supervisors/commissioners/select boards. STILL MISSING: term dates (the CSV carries none - needs the API or the openstates/people YAML), and photos (Plural publishes an image URL; not shipped because it would be a hotlink of unknown licence - D20). QUOTA RECORDED 2026-08-12, branch claude/plural-quota-and-vendor-note, test (132 pass) lint build all green. Plural free tier is 500 GraphQL requests/day at 1 req/sec. THIS IS A QUOTA, NOT A TERMS RESTRICTION - it limits how we build, not whether we may, so D03 STAYS CLEARED. It is also the reason the bulk route is correct rather than merely preferred: 620 legislators across AZ/NJ/NH under any per-person or per-district GraphQL pattern would spend most of a day allowance in one build and do it again on every rerun. The bulk route costs 3 static requests, metered against nothing. The build now PRINTS both counters separately every run - "requests: 3 bulk (unmetered) / 0 GraphQL of 500/day" - and warns above 50% of the ceiling, so the limit is a visible number rather than something discovered by hitting a 429. Counters are kept apart deliberately: adding static bulk downloads to the GraphQL count would invent pressure on a ceiling nothing is near. tests/plural.test.ts gained a regression guard asserting bulkUrl points at data.openstates.org and NOT at the API host, because the likely way this breaks is someone reaching for GraphQL to fill in term dates, which the CSV lacks. If GraphQL is ever needed: serialize at 1 req/sec, cache hard, never re-fetch unchanged, print the count. Written up in docs/vendor-review.md as a fourth section, framed as the different kind of entry it is - Plural PUBLISHES public-domain data rather than holding a public body records, so there is no access question of the sort Granicus/Hyland/Diligent raise, and CC-0 means it is the only source in that document with no commercial-use question at all.

Item: MapLibre vector tile fix
Detail: Turbopack raw-copies maplibre-gl-worker.mjs without rewriting its import of maplibre-gl-shared.mjs, so the worker 404s and no .pbf is ever fetched. Vendor both files into public/ so the relative import resolves, then delete the raster branch.
Notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-11 - see the RESOLUTION paragraph at the end; the diagnosis before it was partly wrong and is kept for the record. NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_RASTER=1 is a workaround that contradicts CLAUDE.md line 12 and must not ship. Re-vendor on every maplibre-gl upgrade. Also widen the error filter in map-canvas.tsx - it currently swallows anything not matching /style|sprite|glyphs|tile/i, including Failed to fetch. 2026-08-11 diagnosis only, fix NOT applied. Root cause confirmed in a production build, so it is not dev-only and the earlier React Strict Mode theory is retracted: the worker script itself serves 200, but its first statement imports ./maplibre-gl-shared.mjs, which 404s - Turbopack copies the worker into /_next/static/media/ byte-identical (verified by file hash) without rewriting the specifier, while emitting the sibling content-hashed as maplibre-gl-shared.<hash>.mjs. Module evaluation fails, the Worker error event carries an empty message that MapLibre never surfaces, and 0 .pbf requests are ever made while style.json, tiles.json and sprite all return 200. Evidence: resource timing on localhost:3000 production build, pbf=0. Also landed this session: CARTO silent fallback removed - buildRasterStyle returns null without a key and the caller shows the Basemap unavailable notice rather than substituting a provider; must-not-ship note added at the top of lib/map/style.ts citing CLAUDE.md line 12; basemap style pinned to basic-v2-dark. Two things to undo when the raster branch is deleted: (1) buildRasterStyle() now sets a glyphs endpoint, which exists only so the district label layer has fonts on the raster path - the vector style defines its own glyphs, so remove it with the branch rather than carrying it over. (2) firstSymbolLayerId in lib/map/districts.ts returns undefined in raster mode because that style has no symbol layers, so the beforeId insertion is inert and the district layers simply append on top; once vector rendering is restored, verify the ordering actually works and that basemap place names draw above the district boundaries. RESOLUTION 2026-08-11: two independent root causes, not one. (1) The worker. The Turbopack-specific part of the diagnosis above was too narrow - maplibre-gl 6 locates its worker at runtime via new URL(template, import.meta.url) built from a variable, which is not the static form any bundler rewrites, so webpack fails identically. Verified empirically: next dev --webpack still yields 0 .pbf and the same MIME-type error, so the webpack escape hatch was ruled out rather than assumed. Fix is scripts/build-map-worker.mjs, an esbuild step that bundles the worker and its shared sibling into one self-contained 461 KB public/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs, wired to predev and prebuild so it regenerates on every maplibre-gl upgrade instead of drifting; the file is now gitignored and untracked, since a committed copy is exactly what goes stale. The script asserts the bundle has no unresolved imports left and fails the build if it does. (2) The district overlay had a second, unrelated cause that would have survived the worker fix. Attachment waited on map.once(idle), and idle requires style.loaded(), which requires every source to report loaded - but the MapTiler styles declare a maptiler_attribution source that is a vector source carrying only an attribution string, with no url, no tiles, and no layer referencing it. It has nothing to fetch, so its loaded flag is false forever, map.loaded() is never true, and idle never fires. Attachment now waits on getStyle().layers, the public signal that the stylesheet is parsed, which is the only precondition addSource and addLayer actually have. Evidence, measured in-page: 6 basemap tiles fetched from the .pbf template and all 6 parsed into buckets, 557 rendered basemap features across 13 layers including Water, so the land/water edge test passes; districts draw with 6 geojson-vt tiles, 11 rendered features, labels AZ-7 and AZ-6, ocdId ocd-division/country:us/state:az/cd:7. Note that .pbf fetches originate inside the worker and are invisible to main-thread resource timing, which is why the earlier pbf=0 evidence could not distinguish a dead worker from a throttled render loop; tile bucket state is the reliable signal. Raster branch, rasterBasemapEnabled, the NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_RASTER flag and the OpenFreeMap fallback are all deleted; resolveBasemap now returns null without a key and the caller shows Basemap unavailable. The error filter in map-canvas.tsx now logs every MapLibre error and filters only which ones raise a user-facing notice. Branch claude/civic-map-entry-screen-4ey1cs; test (26 pass), lint and build all pass.

Detail: Replace the public-notice palette with EdiaStratMap tokens, swap typography to DM Sans plus JetBrains Mono, and add a persisted light/dark theme toggle.
Notes: 2026-08-11. Ported :root and [data-theme=light] token sets from EdiaStratMap src/styles/main.css. Edia drives its UI from three accents (strat/cust/both); ours are the three government tiers, so --accent-local, --accent-state, --accent-national and --accent-all each with a -glow variant, plus --concluded, --canceled and --district-line. Typography is DM Sans for all UI text and JetBrains Mono for every numeral, identifier, OCD-ID, date and time, both loaded as variable fonts through next/font/google. Theme toggle persists under wtp.theme using the same useSyncExternalStore shape as use-stored-zip (frozen pending snapshot, cached against the raw stored string) and writes data-theme on <html>; an inline pre-paint script in app/layout.tsx applies it before first paint, because no hook runs early enough to prevent a flash. Legacy ink/paper/signal Tailwind aliases are kept in an explicitly marked block so the existing entry screen keeps rendering; they are to be deleted as Phase 2/3 replaces those components. Two things went beyond the brief and are worth knowing. (1) The basemap now follows the theme (basic-v2-dark / basic-v2, both overridable by env). EdiaStratMap does not theme its map, but it does not need to - it draws dark panels over a single light OSM layer, whereas ours is a dark vector style, so a fixed basemap would have put light panels over a dark map. (2) lib/map/districts.ts no longer hardcodes its colours; it reads --district-line and --bg off the document when it builds the layers, so globals.css is the single source of truth. Two real bugs were found and fixed doing this, both in the silent-failure family. A restyle effect written with a skip-the-first-run flag fired a spurious setStyle while the initial style was still loading and wedged the renderer, because React Strict Mode re-invokes effects against the same component instance and the flag reads as already spent on the second pass; it is now keyed on the style URL actually applied, which is idempotent under any number of runs. And re-attaching the district overlay after setStyle with once(styledata) silently lost it, because styledata fires for the outgoing style before the new one is applied, so the guard saw the layers still present, skipped the re-add, and the incoming style then wiped them - light mode came up with no districts and nothing logged. District attachment is now a standing invariant subscribed to every styledata and guarded on wanted-absent-and-parsed, so it self-heals after any style change. Item: Counsel question: vendor terms vs. public records duty
Detail: Can a software vendor's terms narrow statutory access to records a public body must publish?
Notes: For B05. Framing: agendas are made and used by a district in the course of official duty, and open meeting law obliges the district to post them in advance. Live constraint on the whole local wedge, not a formality - the answer determines whether the school-board tier is reachable at all, so it is worth asking early. Item: handoff --ship leaves local main stale
Detail: --ship merges the PR on GitHub but never fast-forwards local main, so local main sits a whole session behind. Checking it out makes the repo look empty.
Notes: Found 2026-08-12 at session start. The working tree was on main at 64fee33 - the initial "Add files via upload" commit carrying only CLAUDE.md - while origin/main was at 2978324 with 26 commits and 118 files. Every phase of work was present and safe on origin; local main had simply never been updated, because scripts/handoff.mjs merges the PR through gh and then leaves the session on the feature branch. Nothing in the repo pulls main afterwards, so it goes stale by one session every time and the next checkout of main presents an apparently empty project. Recovered with git merge --ff-only origin/main: local main held zero unique commits and was a strict ancestor, and none of the untracked files (public/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs, screenshots/, next-env.d.ts, tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, .env.local) collided with a tracked path, so the fast-forward was lossless. 68/68 tests pass on the restored tree. Fix: have --ship fast-forward local main after a successful merge, and have the plain handoff check report main being behind origin/main as a warning - it currently only checks the branch against its own upstream and main against the branch, never local main against origin/main, which is the exact gap that hid this. SECOND GAP IN THE SAME SCRIPT, hit 2026-08-12: --ship refuses outright on a branch that has no upstream yet (ship() returns early on "refused - no upstream to push to"). It assumes the branch was already pushed by hand at some point, which is true for a long-lived branch and false for every new one - so the first --ship of every session fails until someone runs git push -u by hand. It should push -u origin HEAD itself when there is no upstream, which is the same one-line class of fix as fast-forwarding main afterwards. Both ends of the script assume a branch that already exists on the remote. FIXED 2026-08-12, branch claude/fix-r07-fast-forward-main. DONE: test (79 pass), lint and build all green. All three parts of this row are closed. (1) --ship fast-forwards local main after a successful merge, via git fetch origin main:main - it moves the ref WITHOUT touching the working tree and refuses anything that is not a fast-forward, so a diverged main is reported, never flattened. Git rejects that fetch form when main is the checked-out branch, so from main it is git merge --ff-only origin/main instead. It runs after the post-ship re-measure and before git-state.txt is rewritten, so the report and the mirror file both describe the state the session actually ends in. (2) --ship pushes -u origin HEAD when the branch has no upstream instead of refusing; a branch created this session having no upstream is the normal case, and refusing meant the first ship of every session failed until someone ran git push -u by hand. (3) The plain handoff check now reports local main against origin/main as its own checklist line, which is the comparison nothing else made - branch vs its own upstream and main vs the branch both read clean while local main sat a session behind. SAFETY: fastForwardMain refuses when local main is AHEAD of origin/main and says so rather than doing anything, and git rejects the non-fast-forward underneath as a second line of defence. Verified both: with a commit only on local main the check reported "diverged - 0 behind, 1 ahead of origin/main" and a manual git fetch origin main:main was rejected non-fast-forward with the local ref unmoved. Verified in a sandbox with a bare local origin rather than reasoned about: a branch with no upstream got one from --ship ("feature pushed, now tracking origin/feature"); after advancing origin main to simulate the merge, the plain check warned "2 commit(s) behind origin/main - git fetch origin main:main"; that fetch fast-forwarded the ref with git status --porcelain empty afterwards, proving the working tree is untouched. The gh-dependent PR steps cannot run against a local remote, so the full --ship path was exercised for real when this row shipped. The suggested command adapts to where you are standing - git fetch origin main:main from a branch, git merge --ff-only origin/main from main - because the fetch form is rejected for the checked-out branch and printing a command that cannot work is worse than printing none.

Item: Resolve the place/cousub duplicate at build time with FUNCSTAT and CLASSFP

Notes: 2026-08-12, branch claude/coverage-language-and-registry-dedupe. DONE: test (79 pass), lint, build all green. THE BRIEF WAS WRONG ABOUT THE SOURCE. 4.6.0 says Census ships FUNCSTAT and CLASSFP in fields already present on the source files. Measured: the cartographic cb_2025 place and cousub DBFs carry only STATEFP, PLACEFP/COUSUBFP, PLACENS/COUSUBNS, GEOIDFQ, GEOID, NAME, NAMELSAD, STUSPS, NAMELSADCO, STATE_NAME, LSAD, ALAND, AWATER. No FUNCSTAT, no CLASSFP. Both exist only in full TIGER/Line. Fix: scripts/fetch-districts.ts gained an optional tigerLayer per district type; place and cousub now also fetch tl_2025_<fp>_<layer>.zip, parse its DBF only (geometry discarded), and join FUNCSTAT/CLASSFP onto the cartographic rows on GEOID. GEOID is identical across the two releases so the join is exact, not a name match - it matched 467/467, 700/700, 100/100, 80/80, 564/564, 259/259, i.e. 100 percent on every layer, and the script throws rather than writing a file if a join matches nothing. TIGER archives are 0.4-1.1 MB at state scale. FUNCSTAT IS THE WHOLE ANSWER and it is cleaner than expected. Across the six clipped files: A=121 active governments, S=119 statistical, F=32 fictitious. The 32 F rows are exactly the duplicates - Census already marks the row it created only to fill its geographic hierarchy. lib/registry/derive.ts now reads FUNCSTAT first (A/B/C/G govern, F/N/S/I do not, unknown is a named skip reason, absent falls back to the LSAD table). Registry went from 297 to 265 bodies, municipal from 153 to 121. CRITICALLY, THE READ-LAYER STOPGAP HAD THE DIRECTION WRONG. dedupeMunicipal preferred the county-subdivision row; Concord NH is FUNCSTAT=A in the place file and FUNCSTAT=F in the cousub file, so the stopgap kept the fictitious row and dropped the actual City of Concord. Counts were right, identity was wrong, which is worse because every officeholder and meeting downstream joins on that key. dedupeMunicipal is deleted. VALIDATION against the 2022 Census of Governments, now by geometric containment rather than an identifier heuristic (a NJ borough is a flat state:nj/place:* row with no county segment, so an ID-shaped test silently misses 29): Pima AZ 5, Merrimack NH 27, Morris NJ 39, plus 3 counties = 74 exactly, per county not just in total. tests/coverage.test.ts asserts the per-county breakdown, that all 32 fictitious rows are suppressed and only those, that Concord keeps the A row, and that Rockaway borough and Rockaway township both survive as separate governments. Payload cost of the two new properties across 6 files: under 1 KB. Remaining gap is FUNCSTAT=C, consolidated governments with a single set of officials - none occur in the three clip counties; tracker M18.

Item: Mirror comparison is raw-byte, so a line-ending mismatch forces a full recopy
Detail: sameBytes() does not normalize CRLF. Dormant now that both sides are CRLF, but nothing stops it recurring.
Notes: Filed 2026-08-12 and CORRECTED the same session, because the first version overstated it. What was claimed: that the mirror line can never report identical on Windows and recopies all five files every session. That is wrong - after one sync the handoff check reported "mirror 5 already current", and both sides now measure identical (CLAUDE.md 140 CRLF / 140 LF on each side, state.md 1337, tracker.csv 88). What actually happened: the mirror held LF copies from an earlier era while the git checkout produces CRLF, so the first comparison flagged all four as differing, one sync rewrote them as CRLF, and they have matched since. A one-time mismatch that has already self-healed, not a permanent failure. Keeping this open at P3 because the underlying fragility is real: scripts/handoff.mjs line 186 calls sameBytes(from, to) on raw bytes while the divergence check just below it at line 207 does normalize CRLF, so the two halves of the same function disagree about what "same" means. Any future write of the mirror with LF - a different tool, a non-Windows checkout, a hand edit in an editor that normalizes - silently reintroduces a full recopy and a red line on the one gate meant to catch a genuinely diverged mirror. Fix: normalize line endings in sameBytes, or add a .gitattributes pinning the four mirrored docs to LF so the working tree and the mirror agree by construction. The second also stops CRLF churn showing up in diffs. Lesson worth keeping separately: this row was written from one --check run without testing what a sync did, which is the same measure-first failure as the 4.5.1 write-up.

Item: Merge consolidated city-county governments (FUNCSTAT=C) into one body

Notes: Found 2026-08-12 while doing M17. Item: git-state.txt in the G Drive mirror
Detail: A generated sixth mirror file recording where git stood at handoff, so a session that opens on the drive without a current repo can see it.
Notes: 2026-08-12, branch claude/handoff-git-state. DONE: test (79 pass), lint and build all green - the script itself carries no tests, it is handoff tooling and the suite does not reach it. scripts/handoff.mjs writes G:/My Drive/we-the-people/git-state.txt after the fetch and before the mirror sync. Plain text, one fact per line: generation timestamp, branch, local HEAD and origin/main by sha and subject, local main sha, the R07 comparison of local main against origin/main with a behind count (and ahead, when both), clean-or-dirty with a changed-file count, open PR numbers and titles, and the last recorded test count with lint and build status. It is the sixth file in the mirror but the first that is GENERATED rather than copied: it has no repo counterpart, so it is not in the MIRRORED table, is never compared for drift, and is simply overwritten each run. Recorded that way in docs/state.md section 3.5. Purpose is the one gap the rest of the mirror cannot cover - a session that opens with the drive mounted but the repo not cloned or not fast-forwarded, where there is no git to ask. The R07 line is the reason it earns its place: nothing else in handoff compares local main to origin/main (it checks the branch against its own upstream and main against the branch), which is the exact gap that let local main sit a whole session behind while every other line read clean. It takes the last matching line in the file because state.md accretes downward. Written a second time after a successful --ship. The first write happens before the push and merge, so it would otherwise describe a state that no longer exists - the same trap the existing post-ship re-measure of the branch, main and PR lines exists to avoid. Verified by running against a scratch mirror (WTP_MIRROR override) rather than G:, and the not-equal path verified in a throwaway clone with local main reset behind origin/main: reported "no - 8 commit(s) behind". Item: session:start, and a dev server that can be stopped
Detail: Three start-of-session checks and a pid-tracked dev server, so a stale main, a clobbered CLAUDE.md or last session server cannot pass for a working one.
Notes: 2026-08-12, branch claude/session-start-and-dev-server. DONE: test (79 pass), lint and build all green. THREE PIECES, one shared property - the environment lies quietly if you do not look. A stale main looks like an empty repo, a clobbered CLAUDE.md looks like a repo with no constraints, a stale dev server looks like a working build. None announces itself; each presents as a plausible working state that is the wrong one. Recorded as a table in docs/state.md section 8. 1. scripts/session-start.mjs (pnpm session:start): fetch and compare local main to origin/main, printing the commit count and the git merge --ff-only command on a miss (R07); check CLAUDE.md is roughly 10 KB, failing under 1 KB or on the bare @AGENTS.md line with a restore-from-mirror command and NEVER a suggestion to reconstruct it; check port 3000 is free; then start the dev server through pnpm dev so predev runs. Exits non-zero on any failure. --check runs the three checks and starts nothing, which is the form a hook wants since the plain form ends in a server that never exits. A DIVERGED main (commits both sides) is reported separately and gets no --ff-only suggestion, because it would refuse. 2. Dev-server lifecycle. pnpm dev is now scripts/dev.mjs, which spawns next dev and writes its pid to .dev-server.pid (gitignored), removed on any exit it lives to see. predev is check-port.mjs then build-map-worker.mjs: it refuses when 3000 is in use rather than letting Next slide to 3001, naming the occupying pid, whether it is this repo own server, and the kill command. Sliding to 3001 is the failure worth preventing - scripts/shoot.mts targets a fixed localhost:3000, so screenshots would be of the old build AND the old map worker, since predev is where that bundle regenerates. 3. pnpm handoff stops the dev server before syncing the mirror, as its own checklist line. Non-fatal when nothing is running. It will NOT kill on a guess: something on 3000 with no matching pid file is reported foreign, with pid and kill command, for a person to decide. If the port is still held after the kill it FAILS and exits non-zero - a handoff reporting the session closed while something still serves is a false report. TWO THINGS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The pid holding the socket is NOT the pid in the file: Next runs the server in start-server.js, a grandchild of next dev. Measured - file recorded 5544, port held by 5816, and the stale server found at session start was four processes deep (17608 cmd shim -> 27420 next dev -> 23496 start-server -> 25956). So kills take the tree and the file-matches-occupant test is descent, not ===; an identity test would call this repo own server a stranger and withhold the kill that works. Second, dev.mjs resolves next/dist/bin/next and runs it under node rather than through the .cmd shim, because the old "dev": "next dev" put cmd.exe /d /s /c between pnpm and Next and killing a shim on Windows can orphan what it launched. FOUND A REAL ONE ON THE FIRST RUN: session:start --check failed on port 3000 held by pid 23496, a next dev started 16:06 that had survived the previous session handoff - exactly the gap this closes. It reported foreign rather than killing it, because it predated the pid file. All paths exercised rather than reasoned about: clean pass; the real stale server; predev refusal both directly and through pnpm (confirming the && chain works in a pnpm script on Windows and that Next never starts); pid file written on dev and removed when Next was killed underneath the wrapper; handoff --check reporting without killing; handoff killing the tree and confirming the port free; foreign holder warning; and the still-occupied path forced with a decoy pid plus an independent holder, which failed and exited 1. Does NOT close R07. session:start reports stale main and prints the fix; --ship still does not fast-forward, and the handoff checklist still does not warn. 2026-08-13, branch claude/deploy-snapshot-and-demo: the missing half added — session:start now KILLS a stale dev server it can attribute to this repo (pid file match) instead of failing, still fails on a foreign occupant, and after starting waits for / to serve then verifies the port holder descends from the child it spawned, printing the HEAD sha served. Verified live: killed-and-started clean, confirmation line printed.

Item: New Hampshire wording - a missing agenda there can be lawful, not our gap
Detail: NH does not require an agenda at all, so NO_SOURCE_FOUND must not read as our coverage failure.
Notes: Found 2026-08-12 doing the D14 statute review. NH RSA 91-A:2 requires notice of time, date and place posted in two public places or a newspaper 24h ahead, and the municipality website may be one of them - but it DOES NOT REQUIRE AN AGENDA, and a body may take up topics not on one it chose to publish. Compare AZ A.R.S. 38-431.02, which requires the agenda posted on the body website, and NJ N.J.S.A. 10:4-8, which requires it only "to the extent known". The 4.6.6 coverage language currently says we do not have a body calendar YET, which reads as our gap. For a New Hampshire body that can be the body lawful choice and there may be nothing to find. Affects 03255 Newbury and every NH body in the registry. Decide the wording before implementing - misattributing a legal choice to our own coverage is the same family of error as claiming unincorporated without measuring it. 2026-08-12 WORDING DECIDED BY THE AUTHOR AND IMPLEMENTED, branch claude/link-ladder-and-coverage-audit (this row first named branch claude/d17-nh-agenda-wording, which NEVER EXISTED - all of 4.6.10, 4.6.9 and the D17 wording landed on the one branch above; recorded rather than tidied over, same as the D03 slip). Evidence: test (162 pass, 5 new in tests/wording.test.ts), lint, tsc and build all green. lib/registry/wording.ts holds agendaAbsenceNote(). The author asked for a combination of two options - the statutory sentence, but driven per body by the audit rather than applied to every NH body. Text: 'We searched high and low for the agenda, and could not find one. New Hampshire does not require an agenda, and this body may not publish one.' AUTHOR TYPO CORRECTED IN THE OBVIOUS DIRECTION AND FLAGGED AT THE TIME: the instruction read 'NH does require an agenda', which is the opposite of RSA 91-A:2 and the opposite of this row's entire premise. Rendering a statute backwards to a reader is exactly the error this row exists to prevent, so it reads 'does not'. A test asserts the negation survives future edits. GATED ON AN EXHAUSTED HUNT, NOT ON THE STATE, which is the part worth keeping: 'we searched high and low' is a claim about work somebody did, and it is false for the 258 of 265 bodies nobody has looked at. Pairing a statutory excuse with a search that never happened would let New Hampshire law explain away our own backlog. So it keys on coverageStatus NO_SOURCE_FOUND, which per M21 now means an audited exhausted search rather than a default. Outside NH an exhausted search gets the first sentence only, because Arizona A.R.S. 38-431.02 requires the agenda posted and silence there is not lawful. RENDERS FOR NOBODY TODAY - zero bodies are NO_SOURCE_FOUND - and a test pins that, so the wording is decided and in place and the first exhausted hunt is what makes it appear. Status stays Not started because the row is also about auditing NH bodies to the point where this can fire; only the wording half is done. 2026-08-13 GATING SPLIT AND DONE. The two sentences are now gated separately: the statutory sentence (New Hampshire does not require an agenda, and this body may not publish one) is a fact about the law and renders for every NH body NOW, whatever its hunt state; the diligence sentence (we searched high and low) renders only on an audited exhausted hunt, which is still zero bodies. Before the split the exhausted count gated both, so the copy rendered for nobody — including Newbury and Kearsarge, the two bodies it was written for. No new copy invented; both sentences are the approved wording. lib/registry/wording.ts, tests/wording.test.ts asserts the statutory sentence renders for real NH bodies and never claims a search. Branch claude/composite-source-and-reprioritization; test (193 pass), lint, tsc green.

Item: Virtual meetings have no place on a map and are currently dropped

Item: Attribute agenda items to the body that acted, not the meeting host
Detail: A county board sitting as another board is real and live; items must not all record as county-board business.
Notes: The 4.6.9 case, CONFIRMED IN LIVE DATA 2026-08-12 rather than assumed. Pima County Board of Supervisors regular meeting of 2026-08-11 (EventId 1824, 124 agenda items) carries the headings "BOARD OF SUPERVISORS SITTING AS OTHER BOARDS", "LIBRARY DISTRICT BOARD" and "SITTING AS THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS". So the county board sat as the library district board, and a SPECIAL DISTRICT business is inside a county feed - which is the 4.7.6 point that a large share of the 39,555 special districts are reachable through county feeds already in Legistar rather than through 39,555 separate hunts. detectSittingAs() in lib/sources/legistar/index.ts REPORTS these headings and is tested against the recorded fixture, but it deliberately does not attribute: turning a heading into a body needs the named district reconciled back to the registry, and there is nowhere to record the answer until meetings and bodies have a join table (Phase 5.1 meeting_bodies, which the brief already says is not optional). Until then a flood-control or library-district vote would record as county-board business, which is the misattribution this row exists to prevent. Note Pima Legistar exposes only 4 bodies, all Board of Supervisors variants, so the district is NOT separately modelled upstream - the agenda text is the only signal. 2026-08-12 THE JOIN IS BUILT. Branch claude/link-ladder-and-coverage-audit (this row first named branch claude/meeting-bodies-join, which NEVER EXISTED - 4.6.10, 4.6.9 and the D17 wording all landed on the one branch above; recorded rather than tidied over, same as the D03 slip). Evidence: test (157 pass, 10 new in tests/attribution.test.ts), lint, tsc and build all green. lib/meetings/attribution.ts holds segmentAgenda / resolveSegment / meetingBodiesFor / attributionSummary and the MeetingBody row shape, written as the table it will become so the Phase 5.1 migration is a transcription rather than a redesign. Segmentation walks the agenda in order: a sitting-as-other-boards heading opens a region, each bare heading inside it names the acting board, and sitting-as-the-board-of-supervisors closes it. Heading detection keys on EventItemMatterFile being ABSENT rather than on capitalisation, so it does not depend on a clerk house style - CALL TO THE PUBLIC is shouted in caps like the real switches are and correctly does not start a body. THE RULE THAT SHAPES THE FILE: an unresolved heading attributes to NOTHING, never to the host. Falling back to the host recreates exactly the misattribution this row exists to prevent, because the agenda has already said in capital letters that the host is not responsible. MEASURED ON THE RECORDED AGENDA, and it found MORE than this row predicted: Pima sat as TWO special districts on 2026-08-11, not one - the AJO DOMESTIC WATER IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT as well as the LIBRARY DISTRICT BOARD. Item: Marker pool - reuse markers instead of rebuilding them
Detail: Markers created once and reused across filter changes, with visibility diffed rather than the set rebuilt.
Notes: 2026-08-12, branch claude/phase-6-popup-and-modal. Evidence: test (132 pass), lint and build green; verified on screen at 85701 and 85641 (12 markers rendered, selection and filtering intact). lib/map/marker-pool.ts ports buildMarkerPool/rebuildMarkerPool/updateMarkerIcon and the _previouslyVisiblePoolKeys diffing. THE POINT IS THE SPLIT: rebuildMarkerPool runs when the DATA changes and creates/removes; applyVisibility runs when a FILTER changes and touches only the pins whose visibility actually flipped, so narrowing 500 pins to 480 does 20 DOM writes rather than 980. A filtered-out pin is HIDDEN (data-hidden, display:none), never destroyed. updateMarkerIcon mutates an existing element rather than replacing it, because replacing drops focus and these are real buttons somebody may be tabbing through. The click handler reads entry.venue at click time rather than closing over the venue, so a pin updated in place cannot hand back a stale one. applyVisibility RETURNS the number of elements it wrote to - if that ever approaches the pool size on an ordinary filter change, the diffing has stopped working. Built now deliberately: at 34 fixtures this is invisible, and once real ingestion lands there is nothing small enough left to verify a rewrite against.

Item: Key votes: resolve the LAWS half via the congress.gov API
Detail: B15's named remainder. The Senate's roll-call lists publish official long titles, not popular names, so a popular-name search structurally cannot resolve the 20 law rows. The route: congress.gov API (CONGRESS_API_KEY already present) to search each law by title, take its bill number from the official record, then take that bill's roll calls in BOTH chambers - including which of two votes counts where a chamber voted twice (BSCA and OBBBA each name theirs in whichVote). House roll calls come from clerk.house.gov's own per-year XML.
Notes: Recorded 2026-08-15 with the finding that produced it, so the next session starts from the diagnosis rather than repeating it. The 20 explainers are already written and author-reviewable; only the roll-call resolution is open. || 2026-08-15 DONE (the truth session, branch claude/truth-session-0815). 0 of 20 law rows to 18 of 20, and the two that are not are STATED. THE ROUTE, every step of it the official record: (1) the public-law lists /v3/law/{congress}/pub for 116-119 — every entry but the pending one became law, so that is the bounded universe the bill must be in; (2) /v3/bill/.../titles, which is where the reader's name for a law actually lives ('Popular Titles | Inflation Reduction Act of 2022') — an entry resolves to the law whose titles carry its curated popular-name phrase and to nothing otherwise; (3) that bill's /actions recordedVotes, each carrying the chamber, session, roll number and the chamber's OWN url (clerk.house.gov / senate.gov), never one constructed here. No bill number is typed anywhere. THE APRIL 2024 SHAPE, resolved mechanically: the House voted on FOUR separate bills and the Senate voted the four as one vehicle, H.R. 815 — so the enacted law carries the Senate's single vote and NO House recorded vote at all. The four siblings get their House votes through the enacted law's own relatedbills list, matched on the same popular-name phrase; four DIFFERENT House roll calls and ONE shared Senate roll call, which is the render the brief asked for. THE CATCH THIS RUN MADE BEFORE IT SHIPPED, and the reason the selection rule is what it is: matching BSCA's whichVote 'final passage' on the literal words picked House roll 212 — 'On passage Passed 230-190' — which is the House passing its own unrelated Byrne-grant version of S.2938 in May. The vote on the gun law is roll 299 in June, 234-193, when the House agreed to the Senate's amendments. That would have put every House member against a vote on a different bill under the name of the law that made news. THE RULE, stated rather than guessed: passage-and-concurrence questions only (cloture, motions to proceed, motions to table and budget waivers are excluded by text), then the LAST of them by the chamber's own timestamp, because that is the vote on the text that became law; a tie the timestamps cannot break is a miss. The rejected alternative was refusing all eight two-vote entries, which would have left the group emptier than the record actually is while the answer sat in the chamber's own timeline. Also fixed: /\bconcur\b/ matched none of the Senate's own 'Senate CONCURRED in the House amendment' final actions, which is how BSCA and CHIPS first came back as 'no passage or concurrence question' on bills whose concurrence votes were right there. THE TWO MISSES, both correct refusals: funding-fight has no unambiguous popular name among a congress full of Continuing/Consolidated Appropriations laws, and stock-trading-ban has not become law and says so on the card. Guarded in tests/key-votes.test.ts: 18/20 exact (not 'at least'), the chamber's own url per chamber, passage-type questions only with procedural text refused, per-chamber roll-call distinctness (the D40 family, with the April siblings' shared Senate vote as the one legitimate collision), and the BSCA tally pinned at 234-193. New script pnpm law-votes:fetch, with a committed titles cache so a re-run costs a handful of calls. Evidence: test 604 pass (1 new) / lint clean (7 pre-existing warnings) / build exit 0.

Item: The funding-reactions ripcord flips LIVE, and the funding question gets its own five-point scale
Detail: The author's ruling: what is licensed is reader-attention signal (anonymous reactions), never FEC-derived data — a buyer receives opinions about displays, not contributor records. Plus the author's question redesign and the scale-version mechanic that keeps the two instruments apart.
Notes: 2026-08-15 (the truth session, branch claude/truth-session-0815). THE RULING, RECORDED VERBATIM in lib/ripcords.ts and docs/ripcords.md: 'The author rules the exclusion wrong as product truth: what is licensed is reader-attention signal (anonymous reactions), never FEC-derived data — a buyer receives opinions about displays, not contributor records. This is the author's documented, settled position.' The distinction the original framing collapsed: § 30111(a)(4) restricts commercial use of FEC contributor DATA, and a reader's anonymous feeling about a display is neither that data nor derived from it — it carries no name, amount or filing anywhere. ripcord.fundingReactionsInAggregates committed state flips true→false; closer changes from 'Counsel only' to 'Author-ruled 2026-08-15; counsel review welcome and may re-pull it'; the SEPARATE ripcord.fecContributorDisplay question is untouched and still counsel's, asserted as such in the guard. The switch stays as a BELT: provenance tags, filter and pull procedure unchanged, and the test now demonstrates the flag in the position it is NOT shipped in, so a re-pull is one flag and still a filter. THE QUESTION AND THE SCALE (the author's design): both funding controls now ask 'How do you feel about how this campaign is funded?' with Love it / Like it / Don't like it / Hate it / Don't care. The old wording asked the reader to convert a feeling about money into a voting intention — two questions in one button row. The five values go through the server-side validity table and are accepted ONLY on funding targets; the gate runs in BOTH directions, so yes/no/unsure is refused on a funding target too, which is what stops a stale client blending instruments. The control derives its buttons from scaleForTargetType — the same function the server validates with — so it cannot offer a button the write path would refuse. SCALE VERSIONING, the data-honesty mechanic: every row carries scale_version (migration 0003, applied to Neon and verified by column query: integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, 22 existing rows backfilled to 1). Derived server-side from the target type, never sent — a browser does not get to say what question it asked. aggregateReactions keys tallies by (target, division, SCALE VERSION), so a v1 funding tally and a v2 funding tally are two rows, never one: one denominator over both would report a trend caused by the question changing and nothing else. Each tally carries exactly its own scale's columns with zeros and none of the other's, plus the question its own rows were asked — a v1 tally is never relabelled with the wording that replaced it. SCALE_BREAKS dates the break (2026-08-15, 1→2) with a reason a buyer can read. Transparency page rewritten in the SAME COMMIT: the exclusion paragraph is gone because the exclusion is gone, replaced by the simple truth plus the scale break in reader's words ('These buttons asked a yes/no/unsure question until 15 August 2026… never combined'); the coupling guard follows the commitments rather than the wording. Evidence: test 599 pass (3 new + rewrites) / lint clean (6 pre-existing warnings) / build exit 0 / migration verified against Neon.

Item: The Level 1 classifier — the ask box's second rung (6d)
Detail: The keyword matcher refuses on questions a person could route in a second. A model picks WHICH curated topic the question belongs to, out of a closed list — and writes none of the answer.
Notes: 2026-08-15 (the truth session, branch claude/truth-session-0815). BUILT WHOLE, per the brief's 'never half'. THE DOCTRINE, and it is the whole justification: the model's entire output is ONE IDENTIFIER from the curated topic list, or NONE. It does not write a sentence a reader sees — the answer is the same curated route the keyword path assembles, from the same registry and the same sourced people — so the no-generation rule is satisfied structurally rather than by discipline. KEYWORD-FIRST IS STRUCTURAL: answerQuestion reads the classifier's id only after matchTopic returned null, and the guard proves a classifier topic cannot overrule a keyword match. THE CLOSED ENUM IS CHECKED TWICE: as a JSON-schema enum on the wire, and again against TOPIC_ROUTES in readClassifierAnswer — a schema is a promise made by a server, a topic id is a claim about a government. A model answer off the list resolves to NONE, and a topic the routing map does not know still refuses. BOUNDS: ripcord.askClassifier (the author's, product-doctrine not counsel — pulled, the box is keyword-only, which is the complete product it shipped as); a per-day call ceiling (WTP_ASK_CLASSIFIER_DAILY_MAX, default 500) that REFUSES rather than degrading, so an over-ceiling ask gets the answer it would have had; an in-process cache keyed on the question's own normalized words; the log scrub running BEFORE anything leaves, so nothing shaped like a phone number, email or street address is sent. Every failure mode — off, no key, over ceiling, upstream error — returns UNAVAILABLE and the reader sees the honest keyword refusal. STORES NOTHING: the route writes no row, keeps no IP beyond its rate-limit window, and the ask box's own logging is unchanged (topic id on a route, capped question on a refusal) plus a `via: classifier` marker that says which RUNG found the topic — a fact about our machinery, never about the reader. DIAGNOSIS BEFORE THE FIX, both suspects tested: stale .next skipping the type-check is WRONG (a warm-cache pnpm build on the same tree reproduces the failure exactly - compiled in 718ms, then 'Running TypeScript ...', then the identical TS18048); the build ran BEFORE the file existed is RIGHT and is the whole answer - the last pnpm build was in the pre-documents checks, the walk script was written after, and between writing it and shipping only pnpm walk:0815g ran. An ORDERING gap, not a cache bug, which is what decided the gate's home. THE GATE: buildGate() in scripts/handoff.mjs runs `pnpm run build` - the exact command netlify.toml gives Netlify - with tsconfig.tsbuildinfo cleared first, before the first push, and refuses the ship on failure with the TS diagnostic printed (Netlify's log needs the author's login, so a gate that only said 'build failed' would move the wall rather than remove it). NOT tsc --noEmit: tsconfig includes .next/types/**/*.ts, the route types Next GENERATES during a build, so a bare tsc checks whatever they said last time and a bad route-handler signature is exactly what it could miss. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, recorded: a .githooks/pre-push hook - it would catch a push that bypasses handoff, but it is installed by `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` which is per-clone and which session:start only REPORTS on, so it can be silently absent in a fresh clone; and it would fire on every WIP push, which is how a minute-long check gets --no-verify'd away. NO SKIP FLAG, deliberately. PROVEN by injecting a deliberate TS error into the same walk script and running the gate's body against it: refused with 'scripts/walk-0815g.mts(352,5): error TS2532 · Failed to type check.'; tree restored, tsc exits 0. tests/handoff-gate.test.ts guards the WIRING (called before the first push, result acted on, same command as netlify.toml, tsbuildinfo cleared, no skip flag) - a source scan on purpose, since running a production build inside pnpm test would take the suite from 3s to 2min and would be testing Next. Evidence: test 606 pass (2 new) / lint clean (8 pre-existing warnings) / build exit 0; gate green in 9s on the shipping run; PR #44 merged, main 6a6dbbd, production serving it ~4 minutes later.

Item: Turbopack: 'Dynamic filesystem access causes tracing of the whole project' - RECORDED, not built
Detail: One warning on every build, from lib/sources/ballot-curated/index.ts:20. Traces the whole project into three bundles.

VERBATIM: 'Turbopack build encountered 1 warning: ./lib/sources/ballot-curated/index.ts:20:22 - Warning: Dynamic filesystem access causes tracing of the whole project', reported against three consumers: the App Route ./app/api/ballot/scope/route.ts, the Server Component ./app/ballot/page.tsx, and ./lib/ballot/registry.ts. THE CAUSE, unverified beyond the warning's own line number: the curated ballot source's `async fetch()` reads its files by a path computed at runtime, so Turbopack cannot know which files are needed and traces everything. WHY IT IS NOT URGENT: it is a build-time tracing cost, not a runtime defect - builds are 8-9s locally and Netlify's succeed. WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW: whole-project tracing is exactly the kind of thing that is fine until a bundle-size or cold-start limit is hit, and then presents as an unrelated deploy failure. The fix is likely a static import map or an explicit readFileSync of named paths, and the honest first step is measuring what the tracing actually costs rather than assuming.

Item: The extrusion gets sharp: two soft silhouettes replace the grey stroke
Detail: The author, on the NH-coast frames: the raised edge renders as a visible STROKE — a gray band tracing the polygon with every coastal vertex showing.
Notes: 2026-08-16 (g4 item 2), branch claude/apple-clean-0816. The arithmetic confirms the report: the shipped build drew a white line translated [-2,-2] and a black line translated [+2,+2], each 7px wide with 6px blur — 4px apart and 7px wide, so they overlapped over two-thirds of their width and composited to GREY on every side at once. That is an outline wearing a shadow's clothes; one light source gives light on one side and dark on the other. A line layer also traces the geometry, so NH's 256-point coast drew every digitized vertex. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, RECORDED: widening the blur relative to the width — one line of change, and it cannot work, because two opposed strokes on the same path composite to grey wherever they overlap and separating them turns each into its own band. Second rejected alternative: stacking many line layers of decreasing opacity to fake a gradient — buys a gradient for six more layers per state and still traces every vertex. BUILT: a shadow is cast by the SHAPE, so the rise is two blurred SILHOUETTES of the state, offset in screen space, masked to the outside by a FEATHERED mask (a clip is binary, and a binary edge on a shadow that is at ~97% of peak where it meets the shape IS the line). Rings are simplified in SCREEN space at 0.9px, which is zoom-adaptive by construction. The two MapLibre line layers are gone. THE MEASUREMENT IS THE ACCEPTANCE: pnpm measure:extrusion subtracts the effect from its own frame (same camera, chrome hidden in both shots) and reports peak, steepest gradient on 8x8 block means, and the lit/shaded centroid lead. Final numbers, four frames: peak 141/147/168/167; gradient 5.29 / 4.49 / 5.43 / 3.97 per px against a limit of 6; lit centroid leads shaded by 280.2px and 65.7px in dark. THE INSTRUMENT FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS NO SCREENSHOT SHOWED: (1) the mask and both shadows were fed the CLIP path — the viewport rectangle followed by the state's rings, even-odd, which describes everything EXCEPT the state — so the mask was inverted and the thing being blurred was a viewport-sized rectangle with a state-shaped hole in it; (2) the SVG filter regions defaulted to objectBoundingBox -50%/200%, which at neighbourhood zoom is tens of thousands of pixels, and Chromium CLAMPS rather than fades. OPEN AND NAMED: the light theme's lit and shaded lobes measure near-coincident (-22.5px, -3.0px against a +4 floor) — the highlight reads on the author's frames but does not lead by the margin the test demands. Item: The active-state model, built as specified - and the mask stops muting the state the reader is standing in
Detail: The author's g5 item 1. One state active at a time; the WHOLE of it crisp at every zoom; every other state muted and lowered; no state active means no treatment at all. Zip shading removed from the product.
Notes: 2026-08-16 (g5), branch claude/active-state-model-0816. DIAGNOSED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY READING: at the zoom a reader lands on from a zip (z11) the ENTIRE frame was muted and blurred - no crisp pixel anywhere - while the reader stood in the middle of the active state. The mute is a DOM scrim carrying backdrop-filter, clipped to everything-except-the-active-state by clip-path: url(#...). The path fed to that clip was the state's rings projected at FULL EXTENT: measured on production, Arizona at z11 spans x -10869.4..5939.9 and y -16547.3..3432.1, about 16,800 x 20,000 CSS px. CHROMIUM SILENTLY DROPS A CLIP PATH THAT LARGE, and a dropped clip is not a smaller clip - the scrim then paints over its whole box. Proved by holding the TOPOLOGY fixed (viewport rectangle minus one enclosing rectangle, even-odd, an empty region at every size) and varying only the magnitude: +/-2000px gave chroma 17.39 detail 20.15, pixel-identical to the effect-disabled frame; +/-8000px and +/-20000px both gave chroma 11.24 detail 9.57, pixel-identical to the broken frame. Also found: the CSS `mask` on the scrim was INERT the whole time - Chromium does not resolve an SVG <mask> reference from CSS on an HTML element - so the clip was the only thing doing the work and its failure took the entire effect with it. Same class as g4's clamped SVG filter region: Chromium's answer to geometry it cannot rasterize is to drop it, and a dropped mask reads as FULL coverage, the loudest way an ambient effect can fail. FIX: lib/map/state-focus.ts#clipRingToBox - Sutherland-Hodgman per ring against the mask's own region (canvas + FILTER_PAD), applied after projection and BEFORE simplification. Nothing outside that box was ever visible, so the cut removes only geometry that was being rasterized to be thrown away, and it is also the cheapest frame win available. The case that looks identical in the code and opposite on screen is handled explicitly: a ring clipped to NOTHING means the viewport does not touch the active state, so the whole frame is muted (pan into New Mexico with Arizona active) - it used to clear the drawing and render plain, which is the no-active-state treatment. Holes survive the clip, so a viewport inside a hole cancels to nothing under even-odd, which is the truth. ZIP SHADING REMOVED WHOLE per the author's ruling: the tint, both layers, the source, the /api/zcta/<zip> route, lib/geo/zcta-outline.ts and the client fetch are deleted - not flagged off. Committed ZCTA geometry stays in the repo, unused. Its walk check is RETIRED with the feature and replaced by its opposite ('the zip draws nothing on the map'). NEW PERMANENT MEASUREMENT pnpm measure:focus (scripts/measure-focus.mts): the existing pnpm measure:extrusion passed at full marks on this broken build because it measures how SMOOTHLY the edge falls off, not WHAT is covered. The new one is anchored to lng/lat - real places projected through the live map - and asserts interior crispness far from the entered zip (north Tucson, Drexel Heights, the corners of the state), effect-off equivalence with the border excluded by the SHIPPED spec's own reach rather than by a constant, exterior muting compared point-against-itself, per-state data scoping off the network log, and no-active-state at 06716 and with no zip.
